snw-2x03: Stranded in an altered timeline, La'An and an alternate Kirk hunt a Romulan agent in 2023 Toronto and must save young Khan, her notorious ancestor, to restore history.
snw-2x04: Revisiting Rigel VII, Pike's landing party loses memory and identity to the planet's radiation as he confronts Zac Nguyen, a crewman he thought he had lost there.
snw-2x05: When aliens mending him after a shuttle crash strip out his Vulcan DNA, a fully human Spock, helped by Chapel, must face a formal dinner with T'Pring's family.
snw-2x06: Plagued by a sound only she can hear and the frightening hallucinations it brings, Uhura enlists visiting Lieutenant James Kirk to help hunt down where it comes from.
snw-2x07: A time portal drops 24th-century ensigns Boimler and Mariner aboard Pike's Enterprise, where the starstruck pair must be returned home before they disturb the timeline.
snw-2x08: Klingon defector Dak'Rah's arrival stirs M'Benga and Chapel's memories of the war on J'Gal, revealing the doctor's secret past as a battlefield killer and ending with Dak'Rah dead.
snw-2x09: A failed quantum probability experiment sets the crew singing their secrets, and as the field spreads to other ships, Klingons included, Uhura leads a finale to collapse it.
snw-2x10: Answering a Gorn assault on the frontier colony Parnassus Beta, Pike and the Enterprise crew are pulled into open conflict with the reptilian enemy they most dread.
snw-3x01: In the wake of the Gorn assault on Parnassus Beta, Pike and his officers are left facing grave, difficult choices as the fight with the invaders continues.
snw-3x02: During a Federation celebration, an unexpected and unwelcome visitor intrudes on the quiet reckonings Spock and his crewmates are having with their own lives.
snw-3x03: Hunting a cure for the ailing Batel, Pike and M'Benga fly into Klingon territory to the lethal planet Kenfori, where the doctor's war years catch up with him.
snw-3x04: Field-testing an experimental holodeck, La'An steps into an invented detective story and takes on a fictional case that has been built for her alone to solve.
snw-3x05: A search led by Chapel and Dr. Roger Korby brings the Enterprise to a long-dead civilization's ruins, where something sinister lies hidden.
snw-3x06: Lieutenant Commander James Kirk suddenly finds himself commanding the Farragut after a scavenger vessel known as the Destroyer of Worlds overpowers and seizes the Enterprise.
snw-3x07: Helping a planet torn apart by war, Pike and his crew find their every move examined by an inquisitive journalist questioning what Starfleet really stands for.
snw-3x08: Turned into Vulcans by a mission gone awry, several Enterprise officers find the real trouble starts when they try to become human again.
snw-3x09: Marooned on a poisonous moon, helmsman Erica Ortegas can survive only by acting against the convictions she holds most deeply.
snw-3x10: As Pike and Batel ready themselves for her new posting, an old malevolent force resurfaces to menace the Enterprise.
snw-4x01: The Enterprise journeys back to the mass extinction 66 million years ago, finding dinosaurs roaming Earth and, on Mars, a civilization on the brink of destruction.
snw-4x02: A shuttle team investigating a derelict Federation ship adrift like a ghost encounters phenomena none of them can explain.
snw-4x03: A crew vacation on a resort world built for pleasure takes a menacing turn once the planet's promised diversions stop acting like entertainment.
snw-4x04: Mistaken for the leader of a resistance movement, Una Chin-Riley is pulled into an occupied world's fight to throw off Klingon rule.
snw-4x05: Everyone aboard except Spock becomes a puppet after a transporter mishap, and the crew must repel Orion raiders while learning to work their new bodies.
snw-4x06: When disaster hits the Enterprise, separate crises break out across the ship, and scattered teams of crew members each have a single hour to solve theirs.
snw-4x07: Trelane recasts Pike's life as an old-fashioned soap opera, and the melodrama becomes an unexpected means for the captain to examine himself.
snw-4x08: James Kirk finds his career prospects tangled in Starfleet politics that involve both a powerful admiral and his own father.
snw-4x09: An object adrift in space conjures The Kingdom of Elysian, M'Benga's old storybook world, and plunges the crew and their fairy-tale doubles into one shared adventure.
snw-4x10: Caught up in a temporal anomaly, Uhura must work alongside an older version of herself to figure out what is causing it.
st-1x01: Hiding aboard the Discovery, the runaway Xahean queen Po finds an unlikely ally in Ensign Tilly, who shares her struggle with the expectations others place on her.
st-1x02: Waking on the Discovery long after its crew abandoned it, a soldier named Craft bonds with Zora, the ship's AI, who finally lets him fly home.
st-1x03: On Kaminar, young Kelpien Saru rigs a salvaged piece of Ba'ul technology to call out into space, and Lieutenant Philippa Georgiou answers with a way off his world.
st-1x04: Held by a Tellarite bounty hunter, Harry Mudd schemes to avoid being turned in, but this captive is only one of many android copies of the con man.
st-2x01: Trapped in a stalled turbolift on his first day on the Enterprise, Ensign Spock bonds with Number One over questions, Gilbert and Sullivan, and the value of weirdness.
st-2x02: New captain Lynne Lucero's first command, the Cabot, is overrun when stubborn scientist Edward Larkin engineers tribbles to multiply as a food source, with fatal results for him.
st-2x03: Guarding a captive Captain Pike during an assault on Starbase 28, Cadet Thira Sidhu must choose between his pleas and her orders, unaware she is being tested.
st-2x04: A tardigrade named Ephraim lays her eggs aboard Kirk's Enterprise and spends years dodging a zealous repair droid, DOT-7, before the two unite to save the brood.
st-2x05: To ease young Michael Burnham's fear of the dark, her father tells the tale of an ancient African girl whose courage brought stars to the night sky.
st-2x06: The petty feud between schoolgirls Kima and Lil is swept aside on First Contact Day 2385, when rogue synths attack Mars and destroy its shipyards.
tas-1x01: Drawn to a dead star, the Enterprise finds an ancient alien derelict imprisoning a malevolent energy being, which escapes into the ship and must be tricked into leaving.
tas-1x02: Erased from history after a Guardian of Forever mission, Spock poses as cousin Selek on Vulcan to save his boyhood self, though his pet sehlat I-Chaya dies.
tas-1x03: A vast living cloud devouring whole worlds heads for the populated planet Mantilles, and Spock must mind-meld with it to persuade it to turn away.
tas-1x04: Lured by a siren call, Kirk and his male officers begin aging to death under the spell of life-draining women, until Uhura takes command and leads a rescue.
tas-1x05: Rescued from a Klingon pursuit, Cyrano Jones brings aboard supposedly non-breeding tribbles that instead grow enormous, while Koloth hunts for a stolen tribble predator.
tas-1x06: The rescue of long-missing philanthropist Carter Winston delights his fiancée aboard the Enterprise, until he proves to be a shape-shifting Vendorian spy working with Romulans.
tas-1x07: On Phylos, sentient plant beings and Keniclius 5, a cloned Eugenics Wars scientist, abduct Spock to grow a giant copy of him to enforce peace across the galaxy.
tas-1x08: At the galaxy's center, the Enterprise enters Megas-Tu, a realm where magic works, and Kirk must defend the kindly Lucien in a Salem-style trial before its wary inhabitants.
tas-1x09: Back on the shore-leave planet, the crew learns its Keeper is dead and the master computer, tired of serving, is turning the park's fantasies deadly and abducting Uhura.
tas-1x10: Harry Mudd peddles a love crystal he believes is a sham, but when Chapel uses it on Spock, the charm proves real, with volatile consequences.
tas-1x11: A burst of strange radiation shrinks the Enterprise crew to miniature size, the doing of the tiny Terratins, who need help escaping their unstable world.
tas-1x12: Stranded in the Delta Triangle with Kor's Klingon cruiser, the Enterprise finds Elysia, a timeless society of lost ships, and must cooperate with the Klingons to break free.
tas-1x13: On the water world Argo, a sea monster's attack leaves Kirk and Spock able to breathe only underwater, and they must win help from a wary undersea civilization.
tas-1x14: Ferrying a Slaver stasis box aboard the shuttle Copernicus, Spock, Uhura, and Sulu are hijacked by Kzinti who covet the ancient, shape-shifting weapon inside.
tas-1x15: Searching Lactra VII for a missing survey crew, Kirk, Spock, and McCoy are caught by giant telepathic slugs and held as exhibits in their zoo.
tas-1x16: Sent by the Vedala to retrieve the Soul of the Skorr before its theft sparks a holy war, Kirk and Spock discover the thief is on their team.
tas-2x01: When Orion raiders hijack the freighter carrying the drug Spock needs to survive, Kirk must wrest it from pirates who would rather die than be caught.
tas-2x02: Honorary commander Ari bn Bem of Pandro, a being who can split into separate parts, secretly tests the crew to judge whether the Federation is fit for contact.
tas-2x03: After the ship crosses a strange energy cloud, the Enterprise's computer develops a taste for pranks that escalate from harmless gags to trapping officers in the recreation room.
tas-2x04: Arrested on Dramia for a plague that ravaged a colony nineteen years earlier, McCoy must clear himself as the same disease spreads through the Enterprise.
tas-2x05: A winged serpent being who visited ancient Earth as Kukulkan traps the Enterprise, demanding the reverence humans once gave him, until Kirk convinces him they have outgrown him.
tas-2x06: Carrying Commodore Robert April, its first captain, the Enterprise falls into a universe where time runs backward, and April must command as the crew regresses into children.
tng-1x01-02: On the Enterprise-D's first mission, Q puts humanity on trial, and Picard's new crew must prove itself by uncovering that Farpoint Station is a captive shape-shifting space creature.
tng-1x03: A contagion from the research ship Tsiolkovsky, the same intoxicant that once swept Kirk's Enterprise, loosens the Enterprise-D crew's inhibitions just as a collapsing star threatens the ship.
tng-1x04: Lutan, ruler of Ligon II, abducts Tasha Yar to make her his wife, jeopardizing a vaccine the Enterprise needs and forcing Yar to duel his current wife.
tng-1x05: Chasing Ferengi thieves, the Enterprise gets caught with them in the power-draining grip of an ancient Tkon Empire outpost, whose guardian, Portal, puts Riker to the test.
tng-1x06: Warp tests by the arrogant engineer Kosinski fling the Enterprise to a realm where thought becomes reality, and only his alien assistant, the Traveler, can guide it home.
tng-1x07: While the Enterprise ferries feuding Antican and Selay delegates, an energy being picked up from a passing cloud jumps between crew members and ends up possessing Picard.
tng-1x08: On the pleasure-loving Edo world, Wesley Crusher is sentenced to death for trampling a flower bed, and Picard must weigh the Prime Directive against the boy's life.
tng-1x09: Seeking revenge for his son, Ferengi DaiMon Bok gives Picard his old ship, the Stargazer, and uses a mind-altering device to make him relive the Battle of Maxia.
tng-1x10: Q hands Riker godlike power to lure him into the Q, but when his friends turn down the gifts he offers, including sight for Geordi, Riker renounces it.
tng-1x11: Troi's long-arranged marriage to Wyatt Miller brings Lwaxana aboard, but Wyatt's heart belongs to a woman from his dreams, who is aboard a Tarellian plague ship nearing Haven.
tng-1x12: A Jarada scan damages the holodeck while Picard plays detective Dixon Hill, trapping him in 1941 San Francisco with lethal gangsters just before he must greet the Jarada.
tng-1x13: On Omicron Theta, the crew assembles Data's android brother, Lore, who betrayed the colony to the Crystalline Entity and now impersonates Data to feed it the Enterprise.
tng-1x14: Searching the matriarchal planet Angel One for survivors of a lost freighter, Riker finds them wanted as subversives, while a fast-spreading virus leaves the Enterprise short-handed.
tng-1x15: While the Bynars upgrade the Enterprise's computers, Riker is captivated by Minuet, a holodeck woman they designed, as they hijack the ship to save their homeworld.
tng-1x16: Secretly taking a lethal youth drug, aging Admiral Mark Jameson handles a hostage crisis on Mordan IV staged by Karnas, who wants revenge for the war Jameson fueled.
tng-1x17: The sterile people of the legendary hidden world Aldea kidnap the Enterprise's children, and Wesley organizes the young captives' resistance while Picard negotiates for their return.
tng-1x18: At a terraforming station on Velara III, the Enterprise discovers that the tiny crystalline lifeforms in the planet's soil are intelligent and are fighting back against the project.
tng-1x19: Wesley competes for a place at Starfleet Academy in testing on Relva VII and loses to a Benzite, while Admiral Quinn's investigator Remmick scrutinizes Picard's command.
tng-1x20: Klingon renegades rescued from a wrecked freighter urge Worf to join their quest for glory, and he proves his loyalty to Starfleet by killing their leader, Korris.
tng-1x21: On Minos, whose arms dealers died by their own product, an automated weapons demo stalks the away team while Geordi commands the ship against it in orbit.
tng-1x22: The Ornarans' supposed plague cure, felicium, proves to be a narcotic sold by the Brekkians, and Picard undercuts the trade by refusing to repair their freighters.
tng-1x23: Trying to rescue Troi from a downed shuttle on Vagra II, the away team meets Armus, a spiteful tar-like being who kills Tasha Yar on a whim.
tng-1x24: Paul Manheim's time experiments send loops rippling through the Enterprise, and Picard must face Manheim's wife Jenice, the woman he once left waiting in Paris.
tng-1x25: Warned by his friend Walker Keel, Picard returns to Earth and finds Starfleet's top brass controlled by parasitic aliens, whose leader lives inside Commander Remmick.
tng-1x26: As three revived 20th-century humans adjust to the future, the Enterprise investigates destroyed outposts along the Neutral Zone and faces the Romulans after decades of silence.
tng-2x01: An alien presence impregnates Troi with a fast-growing son, Ian, who gives up his life to save the ship, while Wesley, choosing to stay aboard, meets Guinan.
tng-2x02: Holding the Enterprise in a starless void, the being Nagilum means to kill much of the crew to learn about death, and Picard arms the self-destruct in defiance.
tng-2x03: When Geordi asks the holodeck for a foe who can outwit Data, it creates a self-aware Professor Moriarty, who kidnaps Dr. Pulaski and seizes control of the ship.
tng-2x04: Rescuing the charming rogue Thadiun Okona embroils the Enterprise in a dispute between two worlds over a stolen jewel and a pregnancy, while Data studies comedy.
tng-2x05: Deaf mediator Riva, who speaks through a telepathic chorus, loses his interpreters to a gunman's attack and must find another way to broker peace on Solais V.
tng-2x06: Dying genius Ira Graves, who calls himself Data's grandfather, secretly transfers his mind into Data's body, and the android starts behaving like a jealous, arrogant stranger.
tng-2x07: The Lantree's crew all died of rapid aging, traced to engineered children at the Darwin station, and when Pulaski is infected, only the transporter can restore her.
tng-2x08: On an officer exchange aboard the Klingon ship Pagh, Riker must outwit Captain Kargan, who blames the Enterprise for a hull-eating bacterium and readies an attack.
tng-2x09: When cyberneticist Bruce Maddox moves to dismantle Data, Picard wins the android the right to refuse at a hearing where Riker is forced to argue against him.
tng-2x10: Wesley falls for Salia, the young ruler being taken home to unite war-torn Daled IV, only to learn she and her fierce guardian Anya are shape-shifters.
tng-2x11: Iconian software that destroyed the Yamato spreads to the Enterprise and to a nearby Romulan warship, and Picard must search Iconia's ruins for a way to purge it.
tng-2x12: Riker, Worf, and Data are trapped in a casino hotel that aliens copied from a pulp novel for a lost 21st-century astronaut, until they play out its plot.
tng-2x13: A shuttle turns up carrying a dazed second Picard, displaced six hours from the future, and the captain must break the cycle that ends with his ship destroyed.
tng-2x14: Offered command of the Aries, Riker confronts years of resentment toward his father Kyle before turning the post down, while Worf's friends stage a painful Klingon rite.
tng-2x15: Data befriends Sarjenka, a child on the collapsing world Drema IV, by radio, and after a Prime Directive debate the crew saves her planet and wipes her memory.
tng-2x16: To prove humanity isn't ready for what lies ahead, Q flings the Enterprise 7,000 light-years into the path of the Borg, and Picard must ask him for help.
tng-2x17: Picard confides the story of his artificial heart to Wesley while traveling for risky surgery, as the dim-seeming Pakleds kidnap Geordi to extract Federation technology.
tng-2x18: Rescuing Bringloidi farmers from solar flares, the Enterprise finds their sister colony of Mariposan clones degrading, and Picard brokers a merger of the two groups.
tng-2x19: Going through the Betazoid Phase, Lwaxana Troi hunts for a husband and fixes on Picard, who hides in the holodeck, until she exposes two Antedean delegates as assassins.
tng-2x20: Half-Klingon envoy K'Ehleyr, Worf's former lover, helps him face down the T'Ong, a sleeper ship whose crew wakes believing the war never ended, by posing as its commanders.
tng-2x21: Refereed by the Zakdorn strategist Kolrami, a war game pits Riker in the aged Hathaway against Picard's Enterprise, until a Ferengi attack forces a desperate bluff.
tng-2x22: Stung by an alien vine on Surata IV, Riker lies near death as Pulaski drives the infection back by forcing him to relive his most painful memories.
tng-3x01: Wesley's escaped nanites evolve into a thinking colony inside the ship's computer, endangering the Enterprise and Dr. Paul Stubbs's long-awaited stellar experiment, until Data brokers a truce.
tng-3x02: Data must persuade 15,000 stubborn colonists on Tau Cygna V to evacuate while Picard stalls the Sheliak, who own the planet by treaty and will exterminate them.
tng-3x03: An elderly couple are the only survivors on devastated Rana IV, and Picard learns the husband, Kevin Uxbridge, is a godlike Douwd who erased a species in grief.
tng-3x04: When proto-Vulcan Mintakans glimpse a hidden observation post, they start worshipping Picard, who must prove he is mortal, even taking an arrow to do so.
tng-3x05: After archaeologist Marla Aster dies on Worf's away mission, an alien re-creates her for her orphaned son Jeremy, and Worf offers the boy a Klingon bond of kinship.
tng-3x06: With the Enterprise snared by the ancient trap that doomed a Promellian cruiser, Geordi conjures a holodeck version of engine designer Leah Brahms to find a way out.
tng-3x07: Stranded on stormy Galorndon Core, a blinded Geordi must team up with a Romulan soldier, while Worf refuses the transfusion that could save another Romulan aboard.
tng-3x08: Troi falls for Devinoni Ral, a negotiator secretly using Betazoid empathy to win rights to the Barzan wormhole, which proves far less stable than advertised.
tng-3x09: Talks between Acamar and its raiding Gatherer clans are threatened by Yuta, a secret assassin avenging a feud, and Riker, who has fallen for her, must shoot her.
tng-3x10: Admiral Jarok defects from the Romulans to warn of a base at Nelvana III, but his superiors fed him false intelligence to lure the Enterprise into a trap.
tng-3x11: Reviewing Angosia III's bid for Federation membership, the crew captures escaped prisoner Roga Danar and learns he is an engineered super-soldier his government imprisoned after its war.
tng-3x12: On Rutia IV, separatist leader Kyril Finn abducts Dr. Crusher to drag the Federation into his people's armed struggle, and Picard soon becomes his hostage too.
tng-3x13: Expelled by the Continuum and made human, Q seeks shelter on the Enterprise, where a selfless act against the vengeful Calamarain wins his powers back.
tng-3x14: Accused of killing scientist Nel Apgar on Tanuga IV, Riker faces holodeck re-creations of conflicting testimony until the crew proves Apgar died trying to kill him.
tng-3x15: The Enterprise-C's leap forward in time rewrites history into a losing Klingon war, and Guinan persuades Picard to send it, with Tasha Yar aboard, back to die.
tng-3x16: Data builds an android daughter, Lal, and resists an admiral's order to take her away for study, until her rapidly developing mind suffers a fatal cascade failure.
tng-3x17: Worf discovers a brother, Kurn, and returns to the Klingon homeworld to fight charges that their father betrayed Khitomer, ultimately accepting disgrace to prevent civil war.
tng-3x18: Aliens studying leadership imprison Picard with three strangers and put a duplicate in his place, whose erratic orders and advances toward Crusher soon unsettle the crew.
tng-3x19: Picard's vacation on Risa is upended by Vash, a scheming archaeologist, as a Ferengi and two time-traveling Vorgons chase the Tox Uthat, a weapon from the 27th century.
tng-3x20: Racing the Romulans to a living ship called Tin Man, the Enterprise relies on Tam Elbrun, a Betazoid telepath who finds in the lonely being a kindred spirit.
tng-3x21: Shy engineer Reginald Barclay retreats into holodeck fantasies starring caricatures of his crewmates, until he helps track down the contamination causing the ship's malfunctions.
tng-3x22: Staging Data's death in a shuttle blast, collector Kivas Fajo keeps the android as a trophy, and Fajo's cruelty pushes Data to the brink of killing him.
tng-3x23: Aging Ambassador Sarek comes aboard to seal a treaty with the Legarans, but his Bendii Syndrome floods the crew with violent emotions until Picard melds minds with him.
tng-3x24: Smitten Ferengi DaiMon Tog abducts Lwaxana Troi, Deanna, and Riker to exploit Lwaxana's telepathy, and Picard wins her back by playing a jealous lover spouting Shakespeare.
tng-3x25: Nursed to health aboard the Enterprise, an amnesiac Zalkonian known as John Doe is hunted by his own people as he evolves into a being of pure energy.
tng-3x26: Years ahead of Starfleet's estimates, the Borg invade, abducting Picard and remaking him as Locutus, which leaves Riker to order fire on the cube holding his captain.
tng-4x01: The Borg, guided by Locutus, annihilate the fleet at Wolf 359, and Riker must retrieve Picard so Data can reach through him to put the cube to sleep.
tng-4x02: Still recovering from assimilation, Picard returns to his family's vineyard in France and breaks down with his brother Robert, while Worf's adoptive human parents visit the Enterprise.
tng-4x03: Called home by Noonien Soong's homing signal, Data hijacks the Enterprise despite a gravely ill boy aboard, and Lore steals the emotion chip Soong made for Data.
tng-4x04: Picard takes in Jono, a human teen raised by the Talarian captain whose forces killed his parents, and after the boy stabs him, sends him back to Endar.
tng-4x05: After Wesley's warp bubble experiment misfires, Dr. Crusher watches crewmates vanish unnoticed by anyone else, until Wesley and the Traveler reach her shrinking pocket universe.
tng-4x06: To rescue a freighter crew held hostage by a faction on Turkana IV, the Enterprise enlists Tasha Yar's sister Ishara, whose friendship with Data hides her own agenda.
tng-4x07: Named Arbiter of Succession by the dying K'mpec, Picard must choose between Duras and Gowron, while Worf meets his son Alexander and kills Duras for murdering K'Ehleyr.
tng-4x08: Riker wakes sixteen years on as captain, with a son he can't remember, in a future that proves to be a fantasy spun by a lonely alien child.
tng-4x09: About to leave for Starfleet Academy, Wesley must keep a gravely hurt Picard alive after a mining shuttle goes down on a barren moon.
tng-4x10: Robbed of her empathic sense, Troi turns bitter and tries to resign, as two-dimensional lifeforms drag the Enterprise toward a lethal cosmic string.
tng-4x11: Data chronicles a day for Bruce Maddox, from learning to dance for O'Brien and Keiko's wedding to exposing a Vulcan ambassador's transporter death as a Romulan spy's escape.
tng-4x12: Convinced the Cardassians are secretly rearming, Captain Benjamin Maxwell of the Phoenix begins destroying their ships, and O'Brien, once his crewman, must help talk him down.
tng-4x13: Con artist Ardra poses as the devil of Ventaxian legend, come to collect on a thousand-year-old contract, and Picard exposes her trickery in an arbitration judged by Data.
tng-4x14: After an apparent wormhole leaves the crew missing a day, Data's evasions arouse suspicion, until Picard learns he ordered Data to hide an encounter with the reclusive Paxans.
tng-4x15: Surgically disguised as a Malcorian, Riker is hurt and exposed on the eve of their first warp flight, and Picard must reveal the Federation to a wary chancellor.
tng-4x16: Geordi meets the real Leah Brahms, married and offended by his holodeck copy of her, as they try to wean an orphaned space creature feeding off the Enterprise.
tng-4x17: Trapped in Tyken's Rift, the crew can't dream and slides into paranoia, while Troi's recurring nightmare proves to be a plea from aliens stuck there too.
tng-4x18: Members of an old Tarchannen III away team, including Geordi and his friend Susanna Leijten, are drawn back to that world as an alien parasite transforms them.
tng-4x19: An alien probe turns Barclay into a genius who wires his mind into the computer and flings the Enterprise to the galaxy's center, where the Cytherians await.
tng-4x20: Noticing Picard's awkward reunion with Vash, Q casts him as Robin Hood and her as Maid Marian, with the senior staff as reluctant Merry Men.
tng-4x21: Retired Admiral Norah Satie's hunt for a saboteur swells into a witch-hunt that targets a part-Romulan crewman, Simon Tarses, and finally Picard himself.
tng-4x22: Lwaxana falls for Timicin, a Kaelon scientist trying to save his people's dying sun, and fights his decision to honor the custom requiring him to die at sixty.
tng-4x23: Dr. Crusher falls for Ambassador Odan, then learns he is a Trill symbiont, which Riker must carry to finish the peace talks until a new host arrives.
tng-4x24: Seized on the way to Risa, Geordi is programmed by Romulans to kill a Klingon governor, and Data must expose the plot and the Klingon envoy abetting it.
tng-4x25: Data attempts romance with Lieutenant Jenna D'Sora by writing a subroutine for it, while a dark-matter nebula causes objects and people to phase out around the ship.
tng-4x26: Gowron's accession sparks a Klingon civil war, and Worf resigns from Starfleet to fight beside Kurn, while a Romulan with Tasha Yar's face backs the Duras family.
tng-5x01: Picard forms a tachyon blockade to expose Romulan aid to the Duras forces, Data takes command of the Sutherland, and Sela reveals herself as Tasha Yar's daughter.
tng-5x02: Stranding himself with Picard on El-Adrel IV, the Tamarian captain Dathon teaches him a language built on myth, dying of a beast's wounds just as they connect.
tng-5x03: Picard reluctantly takes on disgraced Bajoran officer Ro Laren to find the rebel Orta, and she uncovers an admiral's secret deal with Cardassia behind the mission.
tng-5x04: Xenologist Kila Marr, whose son died at Omicron Theta, joins the hunt for the Crystalline Entity, distrusts Data, and destroys the creature just as communication seems possible.
tng-5x05: A quantum filament cripples the Enterprise, leaving Troi in command of the bridge, Picard stuck in a turbolift with three children, and Worf delivering Keiko O'Brien's baby.
tng-5x06: A headset game Riker brings home from Risa enslaves the crew for a Ktarian takeover, leaving a visiting Wesley and Ensign Robin Lefler to fight it.
tng-5x07: When Ambassador Spock turns up on Romulus, Picard visits the dying Sarek, then sets off with Data, disguised as Romulans, on a borrowed Klingon ship to find him.
tng-5x08: Found on Romulus pursuing reunification with Vulcan, Spock joins Picard and Data to foil Sela's plan to turn his mission into cover for an invasion of Vulcan.
tng-5x09: Self-proclaimed 26th-century historian Berlinghoff Rasmussen watches the crew fight to save Penthara IV from an asteroid winter, but he is a 22nd-century thief with a stolen time pod.
tng-5x10: Worf struggles to raise his son Alexander, newly arrived to live aboard, while a test of soliton-wave propulsion runs out of control and endangers a colony.
tng-5x11: Timothy, a boy orphaned when the research ship Vico was destroyed, copes by imitating Data, as the crew learns the Black Cluster, not the boy, wrecked the vessel.
tng-5x12: Ullian telepaths come aboard to collect memories, and Troi, Riker, and Crusher fall into comas after violent recollections, until one researcher, Jev, is exposed as their assailant.
tng-5x13: Saving Moab IV's genetically engineered colony from a stellar fragment requires technology inspired by Geordi's VISOR, and the rescue fractures the perfect society as colonists choose to leave.
tng-5x14: Their memories wiped, the crew follows planted orders to attack the Lysians under a first officer, MacDuff, who is actually a Satarran using them as a weapon.
tng-5x15: Posing as the ghosts of a lost starship's crew, alien convicts possess Data, Troi, and O'Brien and seize hostages in Ten Forward to free their fellow prisoners.
tng-5x16: Paralyzed by a falling container, Worf plans ritual suicide, and his only alternative is a risky, untested procedure from Dr. Toby Russell, whose methods appall Crusher.
tng-5x17: Riker falls for Soren, one of the genderless J'naii, who secretly identifies as female, but her society seizes her and forces her through psychological reprogramming.
tng-5x18: Caught in a loop that always ends with the ship exploding after hitting the Bozeman, the crew breaks free only when Data sends himself a clue.
tng-5x19: After a banned maneuver kills a Nova Squadron cadet, Wesley joins his squad leader Nick Locarno in covering it up, until Picard pushes him to tell the truth.
tng-5x20: Aboard for an arranged wedding to a rigid Kostolain minister, Lwaxana Troi coaxes Alexander into defying Worf's rules, as metal-eating parasites chew through the ship.
tng-5x21: Hosting peace talks, Picard must guard Kamala, an empathic metamorph who becomes whatever her companion desires, and resist their mutual attraction as she goes to her arranged marriage.
tng-5x22: Exploring a nebula, the Enterprise picks up an alien that takes the form of young Clara Sutter's imaginary friend Isabella and turns hostile over how adults treat children.
tng-5x23: Picard plans to turn a rescued Borg youth into a weapon against the Collective, until Geordi's friendship makes the drone an individual named Hugh whom Picard cannot sacrifice.
tng-5x24: Declared dead after a transporter mishap, Geordi and Ro are really phased and invisible, and must find a way to warn the crew of a Romulan sabotage plan.
tng-5x25: An alien probe gives Picard a whole lifetime in minutes as Kamin, a husband and father on the doomed world Kataan, so its vanished people will be remembered.
tng-5x26: Data's five-century-old severed head turns up beneath San Francisco, and the mystery sends him back to 1893, where he meets Guinan, with the crew soon following.
tng-6x01: Posing as actors in 1893 San Francisco, the away team, dogged by a suspicious Samuel Clemens, stops the Devidians from preying on cholera victims and brings Data home.
tng-6x02: Forced to overcome his terror of transporters, Barclay spots creatures in the beam and discovers they are the missing crew of the Yosemite, trapped in the matter stream.
tng-6x03: Ambassador Alkar secretly dumps his dark emotions into Troi to keep his mind clear for peace talks, leaving her erratic and rapidly aging until Crusher fakes her death.
tng-6x04: Rescued from a transporter buffer after 75 years aboard a ship wrecked on a Dyson sphere, Montgomery Scott feels obsolete until he and Geordi must save the Enterprise.
tng-6x05: Riker and other crew members wake exhausted each morning, and a holodeck reconstruction reveals they are being abducted in their sleep by aliens from a subspace realm.
tng-6x06: Q arrives to evaluate Amanda Rogers, an intern unaware she is a Q, who learns the Continuum killed her parents for living as humans and finally joins it.
tng-6x07: A transporter accident turns Picard, Ro, Guinan, and Keiko into twelve-year-olds with adult minds, and when Ferengi seize the Enterprise, the children lead the fight to retake it.
tng-6x08: An experiment linking Data to the computer glitches a holodeck Western, and Worf, Alexander, and Troi must survive outlaws who share Data's looks and strength.
tng-6x09: Data suspects the exocomps, repair robots built for a particle fountain project, are alive, and refuses to sacrifice them even when Picard and Geordi's lives are at stake.
tng-6x10: Picard, Worf, and Crusher raid a suspected weapons lab on Celtris III while the exacting Captain Edward Jellico reshapes the Enterprise, and the mission ends in Picard's capture.
tng-6x11: Captured by the Cardassians, Picard endures Gul Madred's torture and refuses to say he sees five lights, while Jellico mines a hidden fleet to force his release.
tng-6x12: Reawakened by Barclay, Moriarty seizes the Enterprise to force his way off the holodeck with his beloved Countess, until Picard traps him in a simulation within a simulation.
tng-6x13: Geordi falls for Lieutenant Aquiel Uhnari through her logs while she is suspected of murder at a relay station, until the killer proves to be a shape-shifting organism.
tng-6x14: Kidnapped and surgically disguised as a Tal Shiar officer, Troi must bluff her way through a Romulan warbird to smuggle high-ranking defectors to the Federation.
tng-6x15: Given a chance by Q to avoid the youthful brawl that cost him his heart, a dying Picard takes it and becomes an unremarkable, cautious junior officer.
tng-6x16: An informant at Deep Space 9 claims Worf's father survived Khitomer as a Romulan prisoner, and an accident gives Data his first dream, a vision of Soong.
tng-6x17: Held in a secret camp where Khitomer survivors live peacefully beside their Romulan captors, Worf rekindles Klingon tradition in the young, and some choose to leave with him.
tng-6x18: Returning to the evacuated Enterprise for his saddle during a lethal baryon sweep, Picard poses as a barber and battles thieves siphoning trilithium out of the warp core.
tng-6x19: Picard falls for stellar sciences chief Nella Daren over shared music, then must order her into a firestorm on Bersallis III, after which she transfers away.
tng-6x20: Continuing his murdered mentor Richard Galen's work, Picard races Cardassians, Klingons, and Romulans to assemble a puzzle hidden in DNA, revealing that ancient humanoids seeded the galaxy.
tng-6x21: Rehearsing a play about madness, Riker keeps waking in an alien asylum on Tilonus IV, where captors probing his mind blur which world is real.
tng-6x22: Relieved of duty for performing an unauthorized autopsy on Ferengi scientist Reyga, Crusher presses on and proves his metaphasic shield works and that his colleague Jo'Bril murdered him.
tng-6x23: Kahless the Unforgettable appears to Worf on Boreth, but the returned legend proves a clone made by the clerics, and Worf brokers a ceremonial throne for him.
tng-6x24: Returning to Nervala IV, the crew finds Lieutenant Thomas Riker, a transporter duplicate of Will stranded there for eight years, who still loves Troi.
tng-6x25: Heading home by runabout, Picard, Data, Geordi, and Troi find time stopped around the Enterprise, caught in combat with a Romulan ship and seconds from annihilation.
tng-6x26: Borg acting as individuals attack the Federation, and after Data feels anger in battle, he defects to their leader, his brother Lore, who promises him more emotions.
tng-7x01: Picard, captured by Lore's Borg, must reach an emotionally manipulated Data, as Crusher fights a Borg ship with the Enterprise and Data finally deactivates Lore.
tng-7x02: While Iyaaran envoys study the crew, Picard is marooned on a bleak world with Anna, whose obsessive affection turns out to be an alien's experiment in human love.
tng-7x03: Remotely exploring a ship wrecked in a gas giant, Geordi, grieving his mother's vanished starship, meets an alien that takes her form to plead for help.
tng-7x04: Investigating Picard's apparent murder, Riker is taken aboard a mercenary ship raiding archaeological sites and finds Picard alive, posing as a smuggler named Galen.
tng-7x05: Undercover among the mercenaries, Picard and Riker learn they are assembling the Stone of Gol, a Vulcan psionic weapon sought by an isolationist, while Data commands the Enterprise.
tng-7x06: Data's dream program starts producing nightmares that drive him to stab Troi, and the images turn out to be warnings of invisible parasites feeding on the crew.
tng-7x07: Tutoring the telepathic Cairn aboard the Enterprise, Lwaxana collapses into a coma, and Deanna enters her mind to uncover a buried grief: an elder sister, Kestra, who drowned.
tng-7x08: Imprisoned by paranoid Prytt security forces, Picard and Crusher escape with brain implants that link their thoughts, exposing feelings the two have long left unspoken.
tng-7x09: Hekaran scientists Rabal and Serova claim warp drive is tearing subspace apart, and when Serova sacrifices herself to prove it, the Federation imposes a warp speed limit.
tng-7x10: Helping to save Atrea IV, Data meets Soong's former wife Juliana Tainer and learns she is an android replica of the original, a secret he keeps from her.
tng-7x11: Back from a bat'leth competition, Worf slips between parallel realities, in one married to Troi, until thousands of Enterprises converge and he must find his own.
tng-7x12: Admiral Erik Pressman, Riker's first captain, joins the hunt for the Pegasus, which hides an illegal cloaking device, forcing Riker to choose between loyalty and exposing the cover-up.
tng-7x13: Worf's foster brother Nikolai, defying the Prime Directive, hides a village from dying Boraal II in a holodeck, and Worf helps guide them to a new home.
tng-7x14: At her grandmother's funeral on the Scottish-styled colony Caldos, Beverly Crusher is seduced by Ronin, a ghostly entity bound to her family's candle, who wants her next.
tng-7x15: Junior officers vying for promotion puzzle over their superiors' secretive actions, until Ensign Sito Jaxa volunteers for a covert mission into Cardassian space and never returns.
tng-7x16: Amnesiac and carrying radioactive debris, Data unknowingly sickens a pre-industrial village, while Troi seeks a promotion that requires her to send a simulated Geordi to his death.
tng-7x17: An archive hidden in a comet transforms the Enterprise into a D'Arsay temple and fills Data with alien personas, until Picard plays the moon god Korgano.
tng-7x18: Looking into a crewman's suicide, Troi uncovers telepathic echoes of a murder committed during the Enterprise's construction at Utopia Planitia, and begins reliving it herself.
tng-7x19: Crusher's synthetic T-cell treatment for Barclay goes airborne and devolves the crew into primitive creatures, leaving Data and a slowly changing Picard to find a cure.
tng-7x20: Ordered to evict Native American colonists from Dorvan V, ceded to Cardassia by treaty, Picard is defied by Wesley, who leaves Starfleet to study with the Traveler.
tng-7x21: The mysterious K'mtar pushes young Alexander toward a warrior's path to protect Worf from the Duras sisters, and turns out to be Alexander himself, back from the future.
tng-7x22: Still seeking revenge, DaiMon Bok threatens to kill Jason Vigo, a young man he says is Picard's son, though the tie proves to be Bok's genetic forgery.
tng-7x23: A holodeck train ride gone strange reveals the Enterprise is developing a mind of its own and assembling an offspring the crew must help bring to life.
tng-7x24: Sent undercover to lure a Maquis cell into a Starfleet trap, Ro Laren comes to share their cause and finally betrays Picard to join the rebels.
tng-7x25-26: Warned by Q, Picard shifts among his first mission, the present, and a future twenty-five years on to stop an anomaly of his own making from unmaking humanity.
tos-0x01: Answering a distress call to Talos IV, Captain Pike is captured by Talosians who trap him in illusions with Vina, a castaway, hoping to breed humans as slaves.
tos-1x01: Crossing the barrier at the galaxy's edge, Kirk's old friend Gary Mitchell gains godlike psychic powers and contempt for humans, and Kirk must kill him on Delta Vega.
tos-1x02: Threatened by the colossal ship Fesarius and its commander Balok, Kirk bluffs with a nonexistent substance, corbomite, and learns the menace is a test by a friendly alien.
tos-1x03: Rescued con man Harry Mudd brings aboard three women destined as brides for the miners of Rigel XII, whose allure depends on the illegal Venus drug.
tos-1x04: A transporter fault splits Kirk into two men, one gentle but indecisive and one savage, while Sulu's landing party freezes on the planet below until the halves rejoin.
tos-1x05: On planet M-113, a shape-shifting creature that feeds on salt takes the form of McCoy's former love, Nancy Crater, and kills crew members until McCoy shoots it.
tos-1x06: Picked up on frozen Psi 2000, an infection dissolves the crew's inhibitions, sending Sulu fencing through corridors and Spock into tears as the ship's orbit decays.
tos-1x07: Seventeen-year-old Charlie Evans, raised alone by the unseen Thasians, turns his vast mental powers on the crew when he is rejected, until the Thasians return to reclaim him.
tos-1x08: After outposts along the Neutral Zone are destroyed, Kirk duels a cloaked Romulan ship and its honorable commander, as the Romulans' resemblance to Vulcans stirs suspicion of Spock.
